chunks: It was narrated to me by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qashani from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman ibn Dawud from Sufyan ibn U'yaynah from al-Zuhri from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said:
Fever is a good disease. It gives a portion of suffering to every part of the body, and there is no good for one who is not tested.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of fever in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Thawab al-Amal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) characterizing fever as a 'good affliction' because it distributes pain uniformly across the body, serving as a comprehensive test of patience. This narration highlights the Shia theological view that trials are not merely punishments but opportunities for spiritual refinement, implying that a life without testing is devoid of the merit gained through endurance.
